redFirst.basis: regression task, expectRedFirst false: the threshold was raised to a real figure and the already-fixed implementation (BF1.5 floor 8.5/9.5) satisfies it. For information, at MIN_FONT_PX = 8.5 the run failed with 12 errors (narrow er/ersvg and sequences/seq, 8.49px effective printed as 8.5 because viewer.js rounds the svg width to whole px), so the check does bite; I set 8 instead of editing the implementation.

outcome.technical: tests/visual/screenshots.py: MIN_FONT_PX 4.5 -> 8, comment rewritten (no longer cites the 0.5 floor; states it is a legibility requirement, that the 8.5/9.5 floor in viewer.js draws the smallest text (9.5 user units) at about 8.5px, and that 8 leaves room for the whole-px svg width rounding). Tried 8.5 first: failed 12 errors (8.49px effective). With 8: .venv/bin/python tests/visual/screenshots.py exit 0, PASS vs1 (80 screenshots, 0 errors, 1440 and 400 px, light and dark, clean/internal/shared), PASS vs2. Dependant tests/visual/README.md: grep for MIN_FONT/floor/4.5/4.8 found nothing, so still correct. Other names listed (build, main, run, node) are in .agents/skills/node docs and unrelated to this change. node --test not run (own-tests mode, nothing of its own).
outcome.descriptive: The visual legibility check now requires 8px smallest text instead of 4.5px, and passes at 400px against the BF1.5 floor.

testsAdded: vs1 in tests/visual/screenshots.py now asserts smallest effective svg text >= 8px (was 4.5px) at 400px and 1440px; threshold is no longer tuned to the implementation
